title: timeline native rotate+scale
description:
The timeline export's frame loop ran two Kotlin per-frame passes after
the YUV seam went native (302d565): RotationState.rotateRgb888 then
RgbScale.aspectFill — two allocations and two full-buffer walks per
frame. This adds the fused native twin and dispatches the frame loop
through it, the same seam pattern as the RGB->I420 step.

nativeRgbRotateScale (jni_bridge.cpp): rotates sensor-oriented RGB888
upright by orientationDeg (0/90/180/270 CW, any other value identity —
RotationState's else branch) and aspect-fills to the output frame in
ONE bilinear pass: the aspect-fill sample position is computed in
upright space exactly like RgbScale.bilinear (cover scale, symmetric
crop window, center-of-pixel inverse mapping, clamp-to-edge), then the
four integer taps are inverse-mapped through the rotation into source
space (the rotation is a lattice bijection, so integer taps land on
integer sour
